ChangesWords.description: Whether anything changed; with nothing changed there are no words.
ChangesWords.title: ChangesWords

ClearanceNote.description:
A clearance or ATIS copied down in a pilot's shorthand, as written
and as a controller would say it, for the app's clearance reader.

said.description: The same clearance as the controller said it, in words, figures as digits, nothing added.
said.title: Said

written.description: The note as written, line by line, shorthand kept.
written.title: Written

ClearanceNote.title: ClearanceNote

burn.description: The climb's fuel flow, in burn_unit.
burn.title: Burn

rate_fpm.description: Rate of climb, feet a minute, at sea level where the page has several.
rate_fpm.title: Rate Fpm

speed.description: Best rate of climb speed (Vy), indicated, in speed_unit.
speed.title: Speed

Context.description: The pilot's plan, position and record as the app has them.
Context.title: Context

over_50ft.description: Total distance to clear a 50 ft obstacle, in distance_unit.
over_50ft.title: Over 50Ft

DocumentRead.description:
The page read and checked: the read (the engine rule's input, for
the app to edit and ask again), the engine's answer, what could not be
read, and the model. `unreadable` with nothing else where the page
could not be read at all.
DocumentRead.title: DocumentRead

moment_divisor.description: 1000 where the column is moment/1000; 1 where it is the moment itself.
moment_divisor.title: Moment Divisor

ratio.description: Glide ratio, feet forward for each foot down (9 for 9:1).
ratio.title: Ratio

speed.description: Best glide speed, indicated, in speed_unit.
speed.title: Speed

HandbookCheck.description:
handbook_read_check's answer: the items to confirm, every figure in
the app's units, and the airplane form's figures from them.
HandbookCheck.title: HandbookCheck

HandbookFigures.description:
Every figure in the app's units (knots, feet, pounds, inches,
gallons), as the airplane's record keeps them.
HandbookFigures.title: HandbookFigures

HandbookRead.description:
A handbook's performance or weight and balance page, as read:
every figure in the units the page prints, the units named once.
What the page does not show is null or left empty.

burn_unit.description: Gallons, litres or pounds an hour.
burn_unit.title: Burn Unit

cruise.description: Every row of the cruise performance table.
cruise.title: Cruise

cruise_speed_kind.description: What the cruise table's speeds are: KTAS tas, KIAS ias, KCAS cas.
cruise_speed_kind.title: Cruise Speed Kind

envelope.description: The CG envelope's corners, in order going round its outline.
envelope.title: Envelope

landing.description: Every row of the landing distance table.
landing.title: Landing

max_takeoff_weight.description: Maximum takeoff (or ramp, where only that is printed) weight, in weight_unit.
max_takeoff_weight.title: Max Takeoff Weight

speed_unit.description: The speeds' unit as printed: KTAS/KIAS are kt, MPH mph.
speed_unit.title: Speed Unit

takeoff.description: Every row of the takeoff distance table.
takeoff.title: Takeoff

HandbookRead.title: HandbookRead

Index.description:
What the health check reads: the service, the models it asks, and
the planner it asks for figures.
Index.title: Index

LogbookEntryDraft.description:
The gateway's LogbookEntryRequest as the row gives it; `flownOn`
is null where no date was read, and such a row cannot be saved.
LogbookEntryDraft.title: LogbookEntryDraft

LogbookPageRead.description:
A paper logbook page, as read: a row for each flight written on it,
and the page's "total this page" row where it has one (not the amount
forwarded, nor the total to date).
LogbookPageRead.title: LogbookPageRead

date.description: YYYY-MM-DD; null where the day, month or year cannot be read.
date.title: Date

night_landings.description: Night landings to a full stop.
night_landings.title: Night Landings

total.description: Total flight time, hours and tenths.
total.title: Total

NarrativeDelta.description: A piece of the briefing as Claude writes it.
NarrativeDelta.title: NarrativeDelta

NarrativeDone.description: The whole briefing, once it is written.
NarrativeDone.title: NarrativeDone

NarrativeError.description:
Why there is no briefing, in words a pilot reads. It may come after
deltas: a failure once the first line is out cannot change the status
any more.
NarrativeError.title: NarrativeError

NarrativeLeg.description:
What the prompt reads from one leg, checked before a word of it is
sent. The rest of a nav-log leg (its wind, its true airspeed and
density altitude, its fixes) is kept and read where the prompt has a
use for it. A flyable leg (one with an ETE) needs its heading, ground
speed and fuel; an unflyable one needs none of them.
NarrativeLeg.title: NarrativeLeg

NarrativeRequest.description:
The nav log the Brief shows, to be told in words rather than
recomputed. `aircraft_name` omitted means the planner's own default
airplane. `flown`, when sent, says whose altitudes the legs fly:
"custom" for the pilot's own, else the planner's plan of that name.
`altitude_selection` is the planner's reasoning for the altitude
(the nav log's own), read field by field below.
NarrativeRequest.title: NarrativeRequest

NotamWords.description:
The NOTAM words, with the day the planner first heard the NOTAM
feed (`coverage_since`, ISO date; None where it has not yet): the feed
sends what is issued or changed, so the list is what was heard since,
not the whole list for a field (the owner, 2026-11-09). `unchecked` names "tfrs" where tfr.faa.gov did not
answer, so an empty list does not read as no TFRs.
NotamWords.title: NotamWords

NoteCheckpoint.description:
`source` says where the text came from: "saved" is a pilot's own
earlier edit, "generated" a fresh model call, "error" that call
failing for this checkpoint alone (`description` is None then).
NoteCheckpoint.title: NoteCheckpoint

NoteError.description:
A failure that applies to every checkpoint the same way (a bad
key, an exhausted rate limit), sent once.
NoteError.title: NoteError

OralCitation.description:
A passage an answer rests on, quoted word for word (checked), with
its source's title and where to read it.
OralCitation.title: OralCitation

OralEditions.description:
The editions the sources are: the eCFR's issue date and the day the
AIM was read.
OralEditions.title: OralEditions

OralFocus.description: An ACS element the mock oral examines: its code and its words.
OralFocus.title: OralFocus

OralGrade.description:
The student's answer graded: satisfactory, partial or unsatisfactory,
in a few sentences, the key points it missed, and the citations.
OralGrade.title: OralGrade

OralQuestion.description:
One examiner's question (app.oral), its answer and key points, the
citations that survived the check, and the sources to grade from.
`unsupported` where none did.
OralQuestion.title: OralQuestion

OralQuestionRequest.description:
The student's flight in a few lines (the page's own summary of its
plan and briefing), the ACS elements to examine, and the questions
already asked.
OralQuestionRequest.title: OralQuestionRequest

ReadAsk.description:
A photo of a page and what it is of. `image` is the photo's bytes in
base64 (a JPEG the phone's scanner or the browser made, its long edge
about 2,000 px); `today` the app's own date, which a logbook row may
not be after.
ReadAsk.title: ReadAsk

sources.description: The ids, exactly as given, of the sources this sentence rests on; at least one.
sources.title: Sources

text.description: One short declarative sentence a pilot reads in the cockpit.
text.title: Text

Source.description:
The raw thing a sentence can rest on, as the pilot can read it: a
METAR or a NOTAM as sent, a TAF line, a hazard's words, a finding's
line, a debrief figure's line. `id` is what a sentence cites
("metar:KDLH", "finding:fuel"); `label` is its heading on screen.
Source.title: Source

WordsAnswer.description:
A words endpoint's answer: the sentences that passed the check, the
sources they cite (for the pilot to read raw), which model wrote them,
and -- with no sentences -- why the briefer could not be reached, where
that is why. No sentences and no `unavailable` is nothing to say.
WordsAnswer.title: WordsAnswer

post.description:
The answer as events, one JSON object a line: `tool` (name, label)
as each is asked, `text` (a piece of the answer) as it comes, `action`
for each change proposed, `sources` (id, label, text: the raw things
the answer rests on) once, then `done`; or `error` with the reason in
words. The conversation is sent whole each time, the pilot's turn
last; the context is the plan, position and record as the app has
them (AssistantAsk). One billed Claude conversation a question; the
gateway lets signed-in pilots through (SecurityConfig).

The narrative as lines of NarrativeMessage: `delta` (a piece of
the text) as Claude writes it, then `done` with the whole briefing,
or `error` with why there is none. The body is the nav log the Brief
shows -- idents, airplane, cruise altitude and its selection, the
legs -- and is checked before Claude is asked, so a nav log the
prompt cannot read is a 422 naming the field, not an error line.
One billed Claude call a narrative; the gateway lets only a
subscribed, signed-in pilot through, within the month's cap and the
day's allowance (PlannerProxyController).

One "how to spot it" line per checkpoint, as newline-delimited
JSON (each line one CheckpointNoteMessage), so a slow LLM call on
checkpoint 3 does not hold up checkpoints 1 and 2 that already
arrived.

Two different kinds of failure, reported two different ways. A
single checkpoint's own LLM call failing for a reason specific to
it does not take the rest of the stream down -- every other
checkpoint is independent and still worth generating, so that one
gets its own per-checkpoint "error" line and the loop moves on.
GLOBAL_ANTHROPIC_ERRORS is the opposite case: a bad key or an
exhausted rate limit fails identically for every checkpoint, so
it's reported once as a single stream-level "error" (for one
banner instead of the same text repeated per row) -- but the
stream itself keeps going: every remaining checkpoint still gets
its own per-checkpoint "error" line too, just without spending a
call to learn what's already known. A pilot still gets a row to
type a note into for every checkpoint, not just the ones that
happened to come before the failure.

A POST, not a GET: every checkpoint without a note is a billed
Claude call and a write. The caller's own edit is what they see
where they made one; generation only ever fills the shared note.
The route and its checkpoints are asked of the planner before the
stream opens, so an ident that is not one is the planner's 404 here.

The student's answer graded against the question's answer and the
sources it was asked from (`source_ids`, as the question gave them).

One question on one of the `focus` ACS elements, set in the flight
`plan` describes, not one of those already `asked`; its answer from
the sources and the passages it quotes, each checked word for word.
A 503 where the sources cannot be had, a 502 where the examiner
cannot be reached.

A photographed page (`kind`: a handbook's performance or weight and
balance page, a logbook page, a clearance note) read into figures, and
the engine's check of every one: ranges, units and the page's own sums,
each flagged "check" or "wrong" for the pilot to confirm. A page that
could not be read says why in `unreadable`; a reader that could not be
reached is a 503.

What changed in a flight's briefing since the last look ({dep,
dest, stops, then, now}), for a watch that reads the briefing again
every half hour. The changes are found by the planner, and the words
asked only where there is one: most half hours there is none, and no
call at all.

schema.title: Ask

post.description:
A flown flight's debrief ({debrief}) in a few sentences, and a
paragraph for the pilot's instructor written from them. A 422 from
the planner where there is no debrief: the track never flew.

schema.description: The reading's ask, as the planner's POST /api/words/{kind}/sources takes it.
schema.title: Ask

post.description:
The NOTAMs that matter for a flight ({dep, dest, stops, depart}), in
a few sentences: the NOTAMs in force or to come at every field the
route lands at and the TFRs near it, from the planner. With no NOTAM
and no TFR there is nothing to say and no call.

schema.description: The reading's ask, as the planner's POST /api/words/{kind}/sources takes it.
schema.title: Ask

post.description:
Where the risk in a flight is ({verdict, pilot}: the Go / No-Go as
the app has it and the pilot's record). Never "safe": the decision is
the pilot in command's (14 CFR 91.3), and the briefer is told so.

schema.description: The reading's ask, as the planner's POST /api/words/{kind}/sources takes it.
schema.title: Ask

post.description:
The weather for a flight as a briefer would say it ({dep, dest,
stops, depart, ete_min, fixes, leg_min}, as GET /api/briefing is
asked), from the planner's briefing.
